chunks: And I praise Allah and seek His help from the punishment of Satan and his deceitful acts, and (seek) protection from his traps and way-layings.

And I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and His Prophet, and His chosen and His selected one. His distinction cannot be paralleled, nor can his loss be made good. Lands were brightened through him after dark misguidance, overpowering ignorance, and rude habits, and people regarded unlawful as lawful, humiliated the man of wisdom, passed lives when there were no prophets, and died as unbelievers!
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning and significance of the opening supplication in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In the context of Nahj al-Balagha’s advice on governance and social order, this supplication serves as a rhetorical preamble establishing divine authority before addressing political and economic justice. It underscores the Shia scholarly view of the Prophet as the ultimate remedy for 'Jahiliyyah' (pre-Islamic ignorance), framing his mission as a restoration of truth amidst societal decay and moral ambiguity.
